title: Jangjorim Soy-Braised Beef
shortDescription: Lean beef is simmered until safely cooked and fork-tender, shredded, then reduced gently in a savory soy-garlic braising liquid.
culturalContext: Jangjorim is a Korean soy-braised dish commonly made with beef and sometimes eggs or chiles. Cut, broth, sweetness, shredding, and accompaniments vary.
author: {{LEGAL_NAME}}

ingredients.item: lean beef eye of round or brisket

instructions.heading: Prepare raw beef safely
instructions.action: Cut beef on a dedicated board, keep it refrigerated, and wash hands and sanitize the work area.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Pieces are even and remain cold.
instructions.safetyNote: Prevent raw-beef juices from contacting ready-to-eat food.

instructions.heading: Start the simmer
instructions.action: Place beef, water, garlic, scallions, and onion in a pot; bring to a boil, skim foam, then reduce to a covered simmer.
instructions.safetyNote: Open the lid away from your face and use a clean skimming utensil.

instructions.heading: Cook safely and tender
instructions.action: Simmer until beef exceeds 145°F / 63°C, completes a 3-minute rest equivalent in the hot covered environment, and continues until fork-tender.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: A fork enters easily and the thermometer confirms the safety minimum was exceeded.
instructions.safetyNote: The safety minimum does not by itself establish tenderness; test cooking controls the final texture endpoint.

instructions.heading: Rest and shred
instructions.action: Move beef to a clean bowl, rest at least 3 minutes, then shred with clean forks; strain 720 ml / 3 cups broth.
instructions.safetyNote: Use only clean tools and a clean bowl after cooking.

instructions.heading: Braise in soy
instructions.action: Return shredded beef and measured broth to the clean pot with soy sauce, rice syrup, and optional chiles; simmer until seasoned and reduced.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Beef is deeply seasoned and liquid remains for storage.
instructions.safetyNote: Reduced salty liquid is hot; avoid splashing.

instructions.heading: Serve or cool promptly
instructions.action: Serve hot, or divide beef and liquid into shallow clean containers and refrigerate within 2 hours.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Beef remains moist in the braising liquid.
instructions.safetyNote: Cool in shallow containers; do not leave the deep pot at room temperature.

grillSetup: Not applicable; this banchan is prepared on the stovetop or as a seasoned side.
targetInternalTemperature: At least 145°F / 63°C plus a 3-minute rest for whole-cut beef; continue simmering to a test-cook-verified fork-tender endpoint.
foodSafetyNotes: Keep raw beef at or below 40°F / 4°C and prevent cross-contact.
Meet at least 145°F / 63°C plus a 3-minute rest.
Continue to a fork-tender endpoint established by test cooking.
Cool promptly in shallow containers and refrigerate within 2 hours.

allergens.crossContactWarning: Contains soy and wheat/gluten; verify soy sauce labels.

substitutions: Use certified gluten-free tamari only after verifying the label.
Do not change the beef cut without retesting tenderness and timing.
ingredientSourcing: Choose cold intact lean beef from a reputable retailer.
makeAhead: Prepare up to 2 days ahead and refrigerate submerged in braising liquid.
storage: Refrigerate in shallow covered containers within 2 hours and use within 4 days pending qualified review.
reheating: Reheat beef in its liquid to 165°F / 74°C until steaming.
leftovers: Use properly refrigerated leftovers within the approved window.
servingSuggestions: Serve in small portions with rice and fresh vegetables.

faq.question: Is 145°F enough for tenderness?
faq.answer: It is the whole-cut beef safety minimum with a rest, but jangjorim requires further simmering until test-cook-verified tender.

faq.question: Why store it in liquid?
faq.answer: The braising liquid helps protect the shredded beef from drying.
